question: Based on the structured debrief evidence only, what should the hiring decision be?

state_schema.role: title, level, the 3–5 must-have competencies from the rubric
state_schema.evidence: per competency: the strongest observed example and the strongest counter-example, with which interviewer saw it
state_schema.scores: rubric scores per interviewer per competency (not overall vibes)
state_schema.references: if taken: what they confirmed or contradicted
state_schema.risks: gaps, level mismatch, red flags with the evidence behind them
state_schema.process: any missed interviews or untested competencies

criteria.hire: every must-have competency has positive evidence from at least two interviewers and no red flag has evidence behind it
criteria.hire_at_different_level: the evidence supports the competencies at a different level than the role was opened at
criteria.more_signal: a must-have competency was untested or the evidence is split between interviewers — one targeted extra conversation decides it
criteria.pass: a must-have competency has negative evidence, or a red flag is substantiated

on_hold: A close hire/pass is a more_signal outcome by definition — name the competency to test and who tests it. Never decide on the distribution alone; a person owns the hiring decision.
